analysis.title: Tapestry Inc. (TPR): Refreshing our trackers ahead of F1Q
key_insights: GS remains constructive on TPR (Buy) ahead of F1Q27 earnings, but says the pace and cadence of stabilization in Coach North America growth momentum is critical for the stock near term.
Brand trackers show moderation in Coach momentum through September. Coach still screens favorably on several brand health metrics.

Pricing and markdown data are generally supportive: average product prices are above prior-year levels and promotional activity is below historical peak levels, despite a recent uptick in promotional depth.
Kate Spade is in the early stages of a turnaround and is expected to remain a drag on consolidated growth.

Google search interest for Coach is ahead of competitors, with continued interest in Tabby, Brooklyn and Empire. Y/Y search interest is moderating, with several franchises below fall calendar 2025 levels.
Coach net purchase intent and net promoter scores moderated through September but remain above the broader peer set.

Coach store traffic was positive Y/Y in four of the five months since May, including a return to growth in September after an August decline. Web traffic remained volatile across the full-price and outlet banners.

Bloomberg Second Measure adjusted observed sales returned to +15% Y/Y in September after softer summer trends. Growth was supported by both transaction growth and positive average transaction values, consistent with management's view that units and AUR both contribute.

Promotional trackers show higher Y/Y prices in aggregate, with lower discount breadth but higher discount depth. Price-related purchase intent has deteriorated recently and is flagged as an area to monitor.
Purchase intent in the 18-29 cohort weakened through the summer, while the Millennial 30-39 cohort remains strong.

Key questions for the quarter: sustainability of Coach's growth algorithm as AUR and unit growth normalize from FY26 levels, China demand and digital/marketplace contribution, tariff/freight/sourcing headwinds and mitigation, Kate Spade turnaround progress, and Greater China momentum as comps toughen.

GS cut FY27/FY28/FY29 EPS estimates slightly and lowered its 12-month price target to $162 from $169, on a lower target multiple of 13.75x EV/EBITDA versus 14.25x, reflecting modestly slower growth in core Coach.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut to $162 from $169 as the target multiple falls to 13.75x EV/EBITDA from 14.25x, reflecting modestly slower Coach North America growth. Implies 45.6% upside from $111.24.

earnings_insights: TPR F1Q27 (Sep-26 quarter) GS EPS estimate $1.56, not yet reported. Prior-year comparison quarter EPS is shown as $1.32 for the 6/26 column.
GS FY27E EPS $7.92 (from $7.96), FY28E $9.00 (from $9.04), FY29E $10.27 (from $10.32). These are GS estimates, not reported figures. FY26 (6/26) EPS was $7.05.
GS revenue estimates: FY27E $8,521.1mn (from $8,559.1mn), FY28E $9,173.4mn (from $9,212.2mn), FY29E $9,769.1mn (from $9,810.2mn). FY26 revenue was $8,004.2mn.

tension_points.bull_case: Coach screens favorably on brand health. Net purchase intent and NPS remain above peers, prices are above prior year, promotional breadth is below historical peaks, and observed sales returned to +15% Y/Y in September.
tension_points.bear_case: Search interest, NPI and NPS have moderated, price-related purchase intent has deteriorated, discount depth has risen, 18-29 cohort intent has weakened, and AUR and unit growth are normalizing from FY26 levels.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weaker Coach North America growth in F1Q27 results, which GS calls imperative for near-term stock performance.

theme_stances.key_argument: Coach remains one of the strongest brands in the category, but the cadence of Coach North America stabilization is critical for near-term stock performance.
theme_stances.evidence: We believe the cadence and pace of stabilization of Coach North America
